note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up after recent hospitalization for infection concerns, spasms, lightheadedness, and constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021 and discharged on 07/02/2021. During that admission, patient presented with increasing spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. She was febrile in the emergency department with elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. She experienced labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. Concerns were raised for urinary tract infection and she received IV antibiotic therapy. Urine cultures obtained were not impressive. Patient believes her symptoms were primarily due to constipation rather than infection. She notes that after returning home and having a bowel movement, she felt significantly better. Her blood pressure elevation was causing headaches and vomiting prior to admission. Patient currently feels back to her normal self. She has a suprapubic catheter in place. Patient denies pain or discomfort. Doctor notes that weather was extremely hot during the period leading up to hospitalization, which may have contributed to dehydration and worsening constipation. Patient agrees she tends to stay indoors more during hot weather.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current pain or discomfort. Previously reported spasms, lightheadedness, headache, vomiting, and diaphoresis during recent hospitalization, which have resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. History of constipation. Recent hospitalization for infection concerns and constipation (06/29/2021-07/02/2021).

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily for constipation management; doubles dose when not having regular bowel movements. Lactulose as rescue medication for severe constipation. Vitamin C supplements. Multivitamins.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient stays indoors more during hot weather. Takes supplements including vitamin C and multivitamins. Unvaccinated for COVID-19. Does not receive annual flu shots. Describes herself as somewhat homeopathic in approach to health.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal breathing. No abnormal findings appreciated on cardiac or abdominal examination.

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization labs showed white blood cell count of 23,000. Urine cultures not impressive. Patient notes her white blood cell count was normal last year. Doctor notes white count can be elevated with inflammation and constipation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute to chronic constipation: Patient believes recent hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from quadriplegia rather than infection. Current bowel regimen includes daily Miralax and lactulose for severe constipation. Plan to return in 2-3 weeks for updated fasting labs including CBC to ensure white blood cells normalize. Will also obtain cholesterol panel since patient is due for blood work. If white count remains elevated, will consider further workup for other bowel pathology.

2. Quadriplegia: Stable.

3. COVID-19 vaccine status: Patient is currently unvaccinated and hesitant about vaccine due to concerns about unknown side effects and reports of vaccine injury. Doctor counseled patient that she is high risk given her quadriplegia status and respiratory limitations. Recommended vaccine as the only true preventative mechanism for COVID-19. Discussed that supplements are unlikely to prevent COVID-19. Explained vaccines are safe, that side effects are rare, and that vaccinating healthcare providers and 50% of the country supports safety profile. Patient remains hesitant but open-minded and will consider vaccine. Patient states she is young and healthy enough to beat COVID-19 if infected, and notes close monitoring of her health.
